choices.text: The company has no firm obligation to pay dividends to common shareholders.

questions.explanation: Common dividends are discretionary: the board can pass them in a bad year without triggering default, whereas missing an interest payment does. The other three are all disadvantages of equity, since issuance costs are higher, control is diluted, and dividends bring no tax deduction.
questions.explanationJa: 普通株の配当は裁量的であり、業績の悪い年に取締役会が見送っても債務不履行にはならないが、利息の不払いは債務不履行となる。他の3つはいずれも自己資本の不利な点である。発行費用は高く、支配権は希薄化し、配当には損金算入の効果がない。

questions.stem: Assume that Company A and Company B are alike in all respects except that Company A utilizes more debt financing and less equity financing than does Company B. Which of the following statements is most likely to be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Company A has more net earnings variability than Company B.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Company A has more operating earnings variability than Company B.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Company A has less operating earnings variability than Company B.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Company A has less financial leverage than Company B.

questions.explanation: Debt affects what happens below the operating line. Fixed interest amplifies the swing in earnings available to shareholders, so net earnings vary more for Company A. Operating earnings are produced by the business itself and are unaffected by how it is financed, which rules out B and C, and more debt means more financial leverage, not less, which rules out D.
questions.explanationJa: 負債が影響するのは営業利益より下の段階である。固定的な支払利息が株主に帰属する利益の振れ幅を増幅するため、A社の当期純利益の変動は大きくなる。営業利益は事業そのものが生み出すもので、資金調達方法の影響を受けないのでBとCは否定される。また負債が多ければ財務レバレッジは小さくではなく大きくなるのでDも否定される。

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a source of capital used to finance long-term projects?
questions.explanation: A line of credit is short-term, revolving accommodation for working capital; it is renegotiated periodically and can be withdrawn, so it cannot be relied on to fund a multi-year project. Common stock, preferred stock, and long-term debt are the three components of permanent capital.
questions.explanationJa: 当座借越枠（line of credit）は運転資金のための短期・回転型の与信であり、定期的に条件を見直され打ち切られることもあるため、複数年にわたるプロジェクトの資金源としては当てにできない。普通株・優先株・長期債務の3つが恒久的な資本の構成要素である。

questions.stem: Which of the following factors generally does not impact management's capital structure strategy?
questions.explanation: Capital structure is chosen from the risk and cost of financing: business risk determines how much fixed charge the firm can bear, the tax position determines the value of the interest deduction, and management's aggressiveness sets the appetite for leverage. The expected return on assets belongs to the investment decision, which is made separately from how the assets are funded.
questions.explanationJa: 資本構成は、資金調達のリスクとコストから決められる。事業リスクはどれだけの固定的支払に耐えられるかを規定し、税務ポジションは支払利息の損金算入がどれだけの価値を持つかを決め、経営陣の積極性がレバレッジへの許容度を定める。総資産利益率の見込みは投資判断に属する事項であり、その資産をどう賄うかとは別に決定される。

questions.stem: A firm with a higher degree of operating leverage when compared to the industry average implies that the

choices.label: B
choices.text: Firm’s profits are more sensitive to changes in sales volume.

questions.explanation: Operating leverage comes from fixed costs, which do not move with volume, so each additional sale contributes its full margin to profit and each lost sale takes it away. High operating leverage therefore means high sensitivity of profit to volume, which is a form of risk, not of profitability. Choice A is backwards: high fixed costs go with low variable costs.
questions.explanationJa: 営業レバレッジは固定費から生じる。固定費は数量に連動しないため、追加の1単位の販売は貢献利益の全額を利益に上乗せし、失われた1単位はその全額を奪う。したがって営業レバレッジが高いとは、利益が数量に対して敏感だということであり、これは収益性ではなくリスクの一形態である。選択肢Aは逆で、固定費が高いことは変動費が低いことと対になる。

questions.stem: A company has made the decision to finance next year's capital projects through debt rather than additional equity. The benchmark cost of capital for these projects should be

choices.label: A
choices.text: The before-tax cost of new-debt financing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The after-tax cost of debt financing.

questions.explanation: The benchmark is always the weighted-average cost of capital, regardless of how a particular year's projects happen to be funded. Financing sources are drawn in turn over time, so charging one year's projects only the cost of debt would make marginal projects look acceptable and shift the burden onto the equity raised later.
questions.explanationJa: 基準となるのは常に加重平均資本コスト（WACC）であり、その年のプロジェクトがたまたまどう賄われたかは関係しない。資金調達の手段は時間をかけて順に使われていくため、ある年のプロジェクトに負債コストだけを負担させると、限界的な案件が採算に乗るように見え、その負担が後から調達する自己資本に転嫁されてしまう。

questions.stem:
Management of Russell Corporation is considering the following two potential capital structures for a newly acquired business.
Alternative 1
Long-term debt, 6% interest | $3,000,000
Common equity | $3,000,000
Cost of common equity, 10% Marginal tax rate, 15% Alternative 2
Long-term debt, 7% interest | $5,000,000
Common equity | $1,000,000
Cost of common equity, 12% Marginal tax rate, 15%
Which of the following statements is not true if management decides to accept Alternative 1?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alternative 1 is the more conservative capital structure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Alternative 1 provides the greatest amount of financial leverage.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Net income will be less variable under Alternative 1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Total interest expense will be less under Alternative 1.

questions.explanation: Alternative 1 is 50% debt while Alternative 2 is 83% debt, so it is Alternative 2 that carries the greater financial leverage; statement B is the one that is not true. The other three follow from the same fact: less debt makes Alternative 1 the conservative structure, keeps net income steadier, and produces lower interest ($180,000 versus $350,000).
questions.explanationJa: 案1は負債比率50%、案2は83%なので、財務レバレッジが大きいのは案2の方であり、真でないのは記述Bである。他の3つは同じ事実から導かれる。負債が少ないことで案1は保守的な資本構成となり、当期純利益はより安定し、支払利息も少なくなる（$180,000 対 $350,000）。

questions.stem:
Management of Russell Corporation is considering the following two potential capital structures for a newly acquired business.
Alternative 1
Long-term debt, 6% interest | $3,000,000
Common equity | $3,000,000
Cost of common equity, 10% Marginal tax rate, 15% Alternative 2
Long-term debt, 7% interest | $5,000,000
Common equity | $1,000,000
Cost of common equity, 12% Marginal tax rate, 15% Which of the alternatives has the lowest weighted-average cost of capital and how much is the differential?

choices.label: D
choices.text: The alternatives have equal weighted-average cost of capital.

questions.explanation: After-tax cost of debt = interest rate x (1 - 15%). Alternative 1: (0.5 x 6% x 0.85) + (0.5 x 10%) = 2.55% + 5.00% = 7.55%. Alternative 2: (5/6 x 7% x 0.85) + (1/6 x 12%) = 4.96% + 2.00% = 6.96%. Alternative 2 is lower by 0.59%. Note that the higher rates on both debt and equity in Alternative 2 are more than offset by the heavier weighting toward the cheaper, tax-favoured source.
questions.explanationJa: 税引後の負債コスト = 利率 × (1 − 15%)。案1: (0.5 × 6% × 0.85) + (0.5 × 10%) = 2.55% + 5.00% = 7.55%。案2: (5/6 × 7% × 0.85) + (1/6 × 12%) = 4.96% + 2.00% = 6.96%。案2の方が0.59%低い。案2では負債・自己資本ともに利率が高いが、税制上有利で安価な調達源への配分が大きいことがそれを上回って相殺している点に注意したい。

questions.stem: Management of Kelly, Inc. uses CAPM to calculate the estimated cost of common equity. Which of the following would reduce the firm's estimated cost of common equity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A reduction in the risk-free rate.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An increase in the firm’s beta.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An increase in the risk-free interest rate.

questions.explanation: CAPM: cost of equity = risk-free rate + beta x (market return - risk-free rate). Lowering the risk-free rate lowers the base of that sum. A higher beta or a higher risk-free rate raises it, and higher expected inflation raises the nominal risk-free rate, so it raises it too.
questions.explanationJa: CAPM: 自己資本コスト = 無リスク金利 + β × (市場収益率 − 無リスク金利)。無リスク金利の低下は、この合計の土台を引き下げる。βの上昇や無リスク金利の上昇はこれを引き上げ、期待インフレ率の上昇は名目の無リスク金利を押し上げるので、やはり引き上げる方向に働く。

questions.stem: In general, it is more expensive for a company to finance with equity than with debt because

choices.label: A
choices.text: Long-term bonds have a maturity date and must, therefore, be repaid in the future.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Investors are exposed to greater risk with equity capital.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The interest on debt is a legal obligation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Equity capital is in greater demand than debt capital.

questions.explanation: Equity holders stand last in line: they are paid only after lenders, and only if anything remains. Bearing that greater risk, they require a higher return, and that required return is the company's cost of equity. The legal enforceability of interest is the reason debt is safer for the investor, and therefore cheaper for the firm.
questions.explanationJa: 株主は最後尾に並ぶ。貸手への支払が済んだ後に、残りがある場合にのみ支払を受ける。その大きなリスクを負う分、株主はより高い収益率を要求し、その要求収益率が企業にとっての自己資本コストとなる。利息が法的に強制されることは、投資家にとって負債の方が安全である理由であり、したがって企業にとって安価である理由でもある。

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a characteristic of the capital asset pricing model for estimating the cost of equity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The model is simple to understand and implement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The model can be applied to all firms.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The model does not rely on any dividend assumptions or growth of dividends.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is based upon the stock’s actual market price.

questions.explanation: CAPM derives the required return from the risk-free rate, beta, and the market premium. The stock's own market price never enters the calculation, so choice D is the statement that does not describe it. That independence from price and from dividends is what lets CAPM be applied to any firm, including one that pays no dividend, and its inputs are readily observable.
questions.explanationJa: CAPMは、無リスク金利・β・市場リスクプレミアムから要求収益率を導く。その株式自身の市場価格は計算に一切入らないので、当てはまらない記述は選択肢Dである。価格からも配当からも独立していることが、無配企業を含むあらゆる企業にCAPMを適用できる理由であり、入力値もいずれも観測しやすい。

questions.stem: Management of Terra Corp. is attempting to estimate the firm's cost of equity capital. Assuming that the firm has a constant growth rate of 5%, a forecasted dividend of $2.11, and a stock price of $23.12, what is the estimated cost of common equity using the dividend-yield-plus-growth approach?
questions.explanation: Cost of equity = (expected dividend / price) + growth rate = ($2.11 / $23.12) + 5% = 9.1% + 5% = 14.1%. The $2.11 is already the forecasted dividend, so it needs no further grossing up for growth.
questions.explanationJa: 自己資本コスト = (予想配当 ÷ 株価) + 成長率 = ($2.11 ÷ $23.12) + 5% = 9.1% + 5% = 14.1%。$2.11 は既に予想配当なので、成長率でさらに割り増す必要はない。

questions.stem: If nominal interest rates increase substantially but expected future earnings and dividend growth for a firm over the long run are not expected to change, the firm's stock price will

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change, but in no determinable direction.

questions.explanation: Higher nominal rates raise the return investors require from every asset, which raises the discount rate applied to the firm's dividends. With the numerator, the expected dividends, unchanged and the denominator larger, the present value and hence the stock price falls.
questions.explanationJa: 名目金利が上昇すると、投資家があらゆる資産に要求する収益率が上がり、その企業の配当に適用される割引率も上昇する。分子である予想配当が変わらないまま分母が大きくなるので、現在価値、すなわち株価は下落する。

questions.stem: Assume that two companies, Company X and Company Y, are alike in all respects, except the market value of the outstanding common shares of Company X is greater than the market value of Company Y shares. This may indicate that

choices.label: A
choices.text: Company X’s investors expect higher dividend growth than Company Y’s investors.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Company X’s investors expect lower dividend growth than Company Y’s investors.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Company X’s investors have longer expected holding periods than Company Y’s investors.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Company X’s investors have shorter expected holding periods than Company Y’s investors.

questions.explanation: Under the dividend growth model, price = dividend / (required return - growth). The two firms are alike in every respect that would affect the required return or the current dividend, so the higher price for Company X must reflect a higher expected growth rate, which shrinks the denominator. Holding period does not enter the model, because the value of a share is the whole future stream regardless of who holds it when.
questions.explanationJa: 配当成長モデルでは、株価 = 配当 ÷ (要求収益率 − 成長率)。2社は要求収益率や当期配当に影響する点ではすべて同じなので、X社の株価が高いのは期待成長率が高く分母が小さくなっていることの反映に違いない。保有期間はこのモデルに登場しない。株式の価値は将来のキャッシュフロー全体であり、その時々の保有者が誰であるかには依存しないからである。

questions.stem: Which of the following methods explicitly recognizes a firm's risk when determining the estimated cost of equity?
questions.explanation: CAPM contains beta, an explicit measure of the firm's systematic risk, and multiplies it by the market risk premium. The dividend growth model captures risk only implicitly through the observed price, the bond-yield-plus method adds a judgmental premium, and return on equity is a historical accounting result, not a required return.
questions.explanationJa: CAPMにはβという企業の系統的リスクを明示的に測る指標が含まれており、これに市場リスクプレミアムを掛け合わせる。配当成長モデルは観測される株価を通じて暗黙にリスクを織り込むにすぎず、債券利回りプラス法は判断による上乗せを行うだけで、自己資本利益率（ROE）は過去の会計上の実績であって要求収益率ではない。

questions.stem: Assume a firm is expected to pay a dividend of $5.00 per share this year. The firm along with the dividend is expected to grow at a rate of 6%. If the current market price of the stock is $60 per share, what is the estimated cost of equity?
questions.explanation: Cost of equity = (dividend / price) + growth = ($5.00 / $60.00) + 6% = 8.3% + 6% = 14.3%. Choice A is the dividend yield alone and choice B the growth rate alone; the required return is the sum, because a shareholder earns both the cash yield and the appreciation.
questions.explanationJa: 自己資本コスト = (配当 ÷ 株価) + 成長率 = ($5.00 ÷ $60.00) + 6% = 8.3% + 6% = 14.3%。選択肢Aは配当利回りだけ、選択肢Bは成長率だけである。株主は現金の利回りと値上がりの両方を得るのだから、要求収益率はその合計となる。

questions.stem: The bond-yield-plus approach to estimating the cost of common equity involves adding a risk premium of 3% to 5% to the firm's
questions.explanation: The method starts from what the firm already pays its own long-term lenders, which embeds the market's view of its risk, and adds 3% to 5% for the extra risk equity holders bear over bondholders. Short-term debt is too sensitive to current conditions, and the two return measures are accounting outcomes rather than market-required rates.
questions.explanationJa: この方法は、企業が自社の長期債権者に実際に支払っている利回りを出発点とする。そこには市場が見たその企業のリスクが織り込まれている。これに、株主が社債権者より多く負うリスクの分として3〜5%を上乗せする。短期債務は足元の市況に左右されすぎ、2つの収益率指標は市場が要求する率ではなく会計上の結果である。

questions.stem: In practice, dividends

choices.label: A
choices.text: Usually exhibit greater stability than earnings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tend to be a lower percentage of earnings for mature firms.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Are usually changed every year to reflect earnings changes.

questions.explanation: Boards set dividends with an eye to what they can sustain, raising them only when higher earnings look permanent and cutting only under real pressure, because a cut is read as a signal of trouble. Dividends therefore smooth out the year-to-year swings in earnings, and mature firms with fewer investment opportunities pay out a higher, not lower, percentage.
questions.explanationJa: 取締役会は維持できる水準を見据えて配当を決める。増配するのは増益が恒久的だと見込めるときだけであり、減配するのは本当に追い込まれたときだけである。減配は経営難のシグナルと受け取られるからである。したがって配当は利益の年々の振れをならすことになり、投資機会の少ない成熟企業は配当性向が低くではなく高くなる。

questions.stem:
DQZ Telecom is considering a project for the coming year that will cost $50 million. DQZ plans to use the following combination of debt and equity to finance the investment.
Issue $15 million of 20-year bonds at a price of 101, with a coupon rate of 8%, and flotation costs of 2% ・ of par.
Use $35 million of funds generated from earnings.
・ The equity market is expected to earn 12%. US Treasury bonds are currently yielding 5%. The beta coefficient for DQZ is estimated to be. 60. DQZ is subject to an effective corporate income tax rate of 40%.
Assume that the after-tax costs of debt is 7% and the cost of equity is 12%. Determine the weighted- average cost of capital.
questions.explanation: Weight each source by its share of the $50 million raised. Debt is $15 / $50 = 30% and equity $35 / $50 = 70%. WACC = (30% x 7%) + (70% x 12%) = 2.1% + 8.4% = 10.5%. Choice C is the simple average of 7% and 12%, which ignores that most of the money comes from the more expensive source.
questions.explanationJa: 調達総額 $50 million に占める割合で各調達源を加重する。負債は $15 ÷ $50 = 30%、自己資本は $35 ÷ $50 = 70%。WACC = (30% × 7%) + (70% × 12%) = 2.1% + 8.4% = 10.5%。選択肢Cは7%と12%の単純平均であり、資金の大半がより高コストの調達源から来ていることを無視している。

questions.stem:
DQZ Telecom is considering a project for the coming year that will cost $50 million. DQZ plans to use the following combination of debt and equity to finance the investment.
Issue $15 million of 20-year bonds at a price of 101, with a coupon rate of 8%, and flotation costs of 2% ・ of par.
Use $35 million of funds generated from earnings.
・ The equity market is expected to earn 12%. US Treasury bonds are currently yielding 5%. The beta coefficient for DQZ is estimated to be. 60. DQZ is subject to an effective corporate income tax rate of 40%.
The Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) computes the expected return on a security by adding the risk- free rate of return to the incremental yield of the expected market return that is adjusted by the company's beta. Compute DQZ's expected rate of return.
questions.explanation: CAPM: 5% + 0.60 x (12% - 5%) = 5% + 0.60 x 7% = 5% + 4.2% = 9.2%. The beta below 1 means DQZ moves less than the market, so investors require less than the 12% market return. Choice B applies beta to the whole market return instead of to the premium over the risk-free rate.
questions.explanationJa: CAPM: 5% + 0.60 × (12% − 5%) = 5% + 0.60 × 7% = 5% + 4.2% = 9.2%。βが1を下回るということはDQZの変動が市場より小さいことを意味するので、投資家が要求する収益率は市場収益率12%を下回る。選択肢Bは、無リスク金利を超える上乗せ分ではなく市場収益率全体にβを掛けたものである。

questions.stem: When calculating the cost of capital, the cost assigned to retained earnings should be

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower than the cost of external common equity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Equal to the cost of external common equity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Higher than the cost of external common equity.

questions.explanation: Retained earnings are not free: shareholders could have received that cash and invested it themselves, so the opportunity cost is the return they require, the same as on new common shares. The one difference is that retained earnings incur no flotation costs, which makes them slightly cheaper than externally raised equity.
questions.explanationJa: 利益剰余金は無料ではない。株主はその資金を配当として受け取り自ら投資することもできたのだから、機会費用は株主の要求収益率、すなわち新株と同じ水準になる。唯一の違いは、利益剰余金には発行費用がかからない点であり、その分だけ外部調達の自己資本よりわずかに安くなる。

questions.stem: According to the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM), the relevant risk of a security is its
questions.explanation: CAPM assumes investors hold diversified portfolios, so company-specific risk can be eliminated at no cost and the market pays no premium for bearing it. Only systematic risk, the part that moves with the market and cannot be diversified away, is compensated, and beta measures exactly that.
questions.explanationJa: CAPMは投資家が分散されたポートフォリオを保有することを前提とするため、個別企業固有のリスクはコストをかけずに消去でき、それを負担することに対して市場はプレミアムを支払わない。報酬が与えられるのは、市場と連動し分散によって消せない部分である系統的リスクだけであり、βはまさにそれを測る指標である。

questions.stem: Hi-Tech Inc. has determined that it can minimize its weighted-average cost of capital (WACC) by using a debt/equity ratio of 2/3. If the firm's cost of debt is 9% before taxes, the cost of equity is estimated to be 12% before taxes, and the tax rate is 40%, what is the firm's WACC?
questions.explanation: A debt/equity ratio of 2/3 means debt is 2 parts out of 5 (40%) and equity 3 out of 5 (60%). Only debt gets the tax shield: 9% x (1 - 0.40) = 5.4%. WACC = (40% x 5.4%) + (60% x 12%) = 2.16% + 7.20% = 9.36%. Reading 2/3 as a 2/3 debt weight, or tax-adjusting the cost of equity, produces the other choices.
questions.explanationJa: 負債／自己資本比率が 2/3 とは、負債が5分の2（40%）、自己資本が5分の3（60%）であることを意味する。節税効果を受けるのは負債だけである: 9% × (1 − 0.40) = 5.4%。WACC = (40% × 5.4%) + (60% × 12%) = 2.16% + 7.20% = 9.36%。2/3 を負債の構成比そのものと読んだり、自己資本コストにも税率を適用したりすると、他の選択肢になる。

If the cost of equity were 12%, then the weighted-average cost of capital under Arrangement #1, to the nearest full percentage point, would be
questions.explanation: Arrangement #1 is 70% equity and 30% debt. After-tax cost of debt = 8% x (1 - 0.30) = 5.6%. WACC = (70% x 12%) + (30% x 5.6%) = 8.4% + 1.68% = 10.08%, which rounds to 10%. Skipping the tax adjustment gives 10.8%, rounding to 11%.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods of valuation provides the most reliable measure of fair value?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use of a discounted cash flow method.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Market values obtained from active markets.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Combination of valuation models and active markets.

questions.explanation: A price struck between willing parties in an active market is observable and requires no assumptions, which is why the fair value hierarchy ranks quoted prices in active markets as Level 1, above any model. Discounted cash flow and other models depend on estimated inputs and are used only when observable prices are unavailable.
questions.explanationJa: 活発な市場で自発的な当事者間に成立した価格は観測可能であり、何の仮定も必要としない。公正価値のヒエラルキーが活発な市場の相場価格をレベル1とし、いかなるモデルよりも上位に置いているのはそのためである。割引キャッシュフロー法などのモデルは見積りによる入力値に依存し、観測可能な価格が得られない場合にのみ用いられる。

questions.stem: A parent company sold a subsidiary to a group of managers of the subsidiary. The purchasing group invested $1 million and borrowed $49 million against the assets of the subsidiary. This is an example of a
questions.explanation: Buying a business with $1 million of equity and $49 million of debt secured on the target's own assets is the defining structure of a leveraged buyout, and because the buyers are the subsidiary's own managers it is more specifically a management buyout. A spin-off distributes shares to existing shareholders rather than selling the unit for cash.
questions.explanationJa: 自己資金 $1 million と、対象会社自身の資産を担保とする借入 $49 million で事業を買収するのは、レバレッジド・バイアウト（LBO）そのものの構造である。買手がその子会社の経営陣であることから、より限定的にはマネジメント・バイアウト（MBO）にあたる。スピンオフは事業を現金で売却するのではなく、既存株主に株式を分配する手法である。

questions.stem: The acquisition of a retail shoe store by a shoe manufacturer is an example of
questions.explanation: The manufacturer is moving forward into distribution, taking over the next stage of getting its own product to the consumer. Combining successive stages of the same supply chain is vertical integration; a horizontal move would be buying another shoe manufacturer.
questions.explanationJa: この製造業者は流通の側へ前方に進出しており、自社製品を消費者に届ける次の段階を自ら取り込んでいる。同一のサプライチェーンの連続する段階を統合するのが垂直統合であり、水平方向の動きであれば別の靴製造業者を買収することになる。

questions.stem: A horizontal merger is a merger between

choices.label: A
choices.text: Two or more firms from different and unrelated markets.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Two or more firms at different stages of the production process.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Two or more firms in the same market.

questions.explanation: A horizontal merger joins firms operating in the same market at the same stage, that is, direct competitors. The other three describe a conglomerate (unrelated markets) and vertical combinations (different stages of production, or a producer and its supplier).
questions.explanationJa: 水平合併とは、同じ市場で同じ段階に位置する企業同士、すなわち直接の競争相手が結合することをいう。他の3つはコングロマリット（無関連の市場）と垂直的な結合（生産工程の異なる段階、あるいは製造業者とその供給業者）を述べたものである。

questions.stem: A soft drink producer acquiring a bottle manufacturer is an example of a
questions.explanation: The bottle maker supplies an input to the soft drink producer, so acquiring it moves the buyer backward along its own supply chain. Combining adjacent stages of production is a vertical merger.
questions.explanationJa: 瓶の製造業者は清涼飲料メーカーに投入財を供給しているので、これを買収することは自社のサプライチェーンを後方へ遡る動きにあたる。生産工程の隣接する段階を結合するのが垂直合併である。

questions.stem: A shoe manufacturing firm acquiring a brokerage house is an example of a
questions.explanation: Shoe manufacturing and securities brokerage share no market, no customers, and no production process, so the combination is a conglomerate merger. A congeneric merger would join firms that are related but not directly competing, such as a bank and an insurer.
questions.explanationJa: 靴の製造と証券仲介業は、市場も顧客も生産工程も共有していないので、この結合はコングロマリット合併にあたる。コンジェネリック合併は、銀行と保険会社のように関連はあるが直接競合しない企業同士の結合を指す。
